result.title: Before the Word: Name Information in Description-Derived States of Small Language Models, With and Without Naming Failure
result.comment: 22 pages, 9 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24228887
result.summary: The tip-of-the-tongue (TOT) state, knowing an object but not its name, motivates this study as an analogy only. We ask whether small language models form a name-predictive state from a name-free description, and whether it differs when naming fails but description selection succeeds. In an internally pre-registered study (a frozen document, no external registry) of Qwen2-0.5B, SmolLM2-1.7B and Phi-3-mini with 200 items, we combine a similarity read-out, a Patchscopes-style read-out and activation patching with matched controls. H1 (name information in the state) was supported in all nine model-by-description-type combinations; the agreement rule was met by the similarity measure together with patching, while Patchscopes stayed near chance. Post-hoc robustness checks after internal review (logit lens, single-position patch, manipulation check) temper this reading: name information in middle layers is clearest under the multi-position patch and the similarity measure, and weak under single-position patching at 50% depth. H2' (description-paraphrase consistency of name-free states not lower in failure items) is mixed: the SmolLM2 deficit test is significant under the pre-registered specification but not robust; Phi-3 non-inferiority holds across margins and a word-overlap covariate, although its bootstrap interval includes zero; Qwen2-0.5B is inconclusive. A capacity explanation remains untested. We report vehicle-level signals only, not meaning.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究以「话到嘴边」为类比，在 Qwen2-0.5B、SmolLM2-1.7B、Phi-3-mini 三种小模型、200 个条目上检验：模型能否从无名称的描述中形成可预测名称的内部状态，并考察命名失败时该状态是否仍与描述复述一致；手段为相似度读出、Patchscopes 式读出与配匹配对照的激活 patching。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本探测，但其相似度读出与 patching 对层深、位置（多位点 vs 单一位点）高度敏感、且不同读出方法结论不一致，可供核查 LVR 中「latent 是否携带任务必要信息」的检验设计与读出可靠性。
